title: Orpheus Country: A Rhodope and Rila Driving Loop from Plovdiv to Sofia

bestPeriod.window: late May to late June for green meadows and full waterfalls, then mid-September to mid-October for colour and empty roads
bestPeriod.avoid: August (Pamporovo and Velingrad full, Trigrad gorge coach traffic) and December-March, when Prevala and the Rila Lakes chairlift road are snowbound

activities.note: €60, €110 (caves, Snezhanka tower, Eagle's Eye shuttle, chairlift)

gatewayAirport: Fly into Sofia (SOF), 1 h 45 by A1 to Plovdiv, or Plovdiv (PDV) direct. Rail Sofia-Plovdiv 2 h. Drop the car in Sofia.
currency: Euro (EUR), sole legal tender since 1 February 2026; mandatory dual BGN display ended 8 August 2026

hook: The Rhodopes are not dramatic in the alpine sense, long, dark, spruce-covered whalebacks with villages in the folds and a road that never stops turning. Then the mountain opens a hole in itself and a river disappears into it. A week of caves, gorges, monasteries and mehana tables, driven at 45 km/h because that is the honest average, and finished on a chairlift above seven glacial lakes.

snapshot.Getting there: Fly into Sofia (SOF), 1 h 45 by A1 to Plovdiv, or Plovdiv (PDV) direct. Rail Sofia-Plovdiv 2 h. Drop the car in Sofia.

itinerary.title: Plovdiv, and the oldest street in Europe
itinerary.morning: Collect the car, then leave it. Walk the Old Town's cobbled ramps, Balabanov House, Hindliyan House, the Roman Theatre of Philippopolis still used for opera.
itinerary.afternoon: The Roman Stadium under Dzhumaya Square, then Kapana, the craft quarter, for coffee. Climb **Bunardzhika**, the Hill of the Liberators, for the Alyosha monument and the whole Thracian plain at your feet.
itinerary.evening: Dinner of *shopska*, *kavarma* and Mavrud from the Asenovgrad slopes at **Gostilnitsa Chuchura** in the Old Town. Confirm the BGTOLL vignette is live on your plate before bed.

itinerary.title: Bachkovo, then the Vacha road
itinerary.morning: **Bachkovo Monastery**, founded 1083 by the Georgian brothers Bakuriani, Bulgaria's second largest, with a 12th-century ossuary and the Virgin Eleusa icon. Buy monastery honey and *katmi* pancakes at the stalls outside.
itinerary.afternoon: North to Krichim, then the reservoir road up the Vacha: 40 km of bends between the Vacha and Devin dams, tunnels, no signal. Arrive **Devin**, a spa town on hot mineral water.
itinerary.evening: Soak in a Devin hotel pool fed by the town springs, then dinner of *cheverme* lamb and *patatnik*, the Rhodopean grated-potato cake that is the region's real signature dish.

itinerary.title: The Devil's Throat and the underworld
itinerary.morning: Drive the gorge into **Trigrad** at 20 km/h. **Dyavolsko Garlo, the Devil's Throat Cave**, swallows the Trigrad river whole: Bulgaria's tallest underground waterfall, about 42 m, in a cathedral-sized hall, with 301 steps cut in rock as the way out. Tradition puts **Orpheus's descent to the underworld** here, and debris thrown in never reappears at the resurgence.
itinerary.afternoon: Back to Teshel, then the **Buynovo gorge** to **Yagodina Cave**, five levels, about 10 km surveyed, a 1,100 m show route at a constant 6°C. Bring a fleece.
itinerary.evening: Take the 4x4 shuttle from Yagodina up the rough forest track to the **Eagle's Eye** platform for sunset over the gorge, then a village guesthouse dinner.

itinerary.title: Shiroka Laka and the bagpipe
itinerary.morning: **Shiroka Laka**: white Rhodopean houses with black timber, the Church of the Assumption of 1834 built in 38 days, and the **National School of Folk Arts**, where teenagers learn the **kaba gaida**, the deep-toned Rhodopean bagpipe, longer-droned and a fourth lower than the thin Thracian gaida.
itinerary.afternoon: Over to **Smolyan** for the **Smolyan Lakes** on the town's northern edge, around eight of an original twenty survive, and the Regional Historical Museum's Thracian and folk-costume rooms.
itinerary.evening: Up to **Momchilovtsi**, a ridge village at 1,200 m famous for yoghurt exported to China, for dinner and the best village views in the Rhodopes.

itinerary.title: Snezhanka, then west to Batak
itinerary.morning: Over the **Prevala** saddle to **Pamporovo** and the walk to the **Snezhanka** tower at 1,926 m, 153 steps to the platform, and on a clear morning the Aegean ridge lines of Greek Thrace.
itinerary.afternoon: Long drive via Devin and Dospat across the **Yavorovets** watershed to **Batak**. Visit the Church of St Nedelya, the memorial to the 1876 Batak massacre, a hard, necessary hour that explains Bulgarian nineteenth-century politics better than any museum.
itinerary.evening: Batak reservoir or on to **Velingrad**. Eat trout from the Batak dam, grilled plain with lemon.

itinerary.title: Velingrad springs to the Rila valley
itinerary.morning: **Velingrad**, the self-styled spa capital of the Balkans: the **Kleptuza** karst spring in the town park pushes out cold water beside eighty-odd hot mineral springs. Ninety minutes in a mineral pool before a long drive.
itinerary.afternoon: The Yundola plateau road to Razlog, the **Predel pass** (1,140 m) with the Pirin wall on your left, then Simitli, Kocherinovo and 22 km up the Rilska river to **Rila Monastery**, UNESCO-listed since 1983.
itinerary.evening: Sleep in a monastery cell or the guesthouses in Pastra below. After the coaches leave at 18:00, the striped arcades and **Hrelyo's Tower** of 1335 are yours.

itinerary.title: Seven Lakes, then Sofia
itinerary.morning: Early liturgy in the Nativity church, then drive to Sapareva Banya and up to **Panichishte**. The chairlift from **Pionerska hut** lifts you to about 2,100 m by the Rilski Ezera hut.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk the cirque: Dolnoto, Ribnoto, Trilistnika, Bliznaka, Babreka, **Okoto**, the deepest cirque lake in Bulgaria at roughly 37.5 m, and **Salzata** at 2,535 m. Three to four hours round trip on rough path; the lakes freeze into June some years.
itinerary.evening: Down the E79 to Sofia, return the car, and finish with *shkembe* or grilled Rhodopean sausage in the Kapana-style bars around Ulitsa Shishman.

accommodationStrategy.name: Rhodopean guesthouse
accommodationStrategy.description: stone-and-timber houses on the Shirokolashka river, wood stoves, *mekitsi* and sheep's yoghurt for breakfast, and hosts who will arrange a bagpipe evening. Parking is on the road, take the compact.
accommodationStrategy.booking: direct by phone or Booking.com, 2-3 weeks ahead; the March *Pesponedelnik* kukeri festival fills the village a year out.

accommodationStrategy.name: Rila Monastery cells / Pastra guesthouses
accommodationStrategy.description: the only way to see the courtyard empty. Cells are spartan, no heating in shoulder season, curfew, cash on arrival.
accommodationStrategy.booking: monastery cells by phone only, 3-4 weeks ahead; keep a Pastra guesthouse as backup.

accommodationStrategy.name: Spa Hotel Persenk
accommodationStrategy.description: enclosed parking, thermal mineral pools fed by Devin's own springs and a restaurant that stays open late, the kind of reset night this drive needs, and Devin sits exactly where the Trigrad and Dospat legs meet. Consistently the highest-rated hotel in the town.
accommodationStrategy.booking: direct or via the usual portals, 2 weeks ahead.

logistics.connectivity: A1 and Yettel cover towns and the main roads; expect nothing in the Trigrad and Buynovo gorges or on the Vacha reservoir road. Download offline maps.
logistics.emergency: 112. Mountain rescue is the Bulgarian Red Cross Mountain Rescue Service (PSS); on the Rila lakes carry the hut's number and tell someone your route.
logistics.weather: Rhodope fog forms fast in the gorges and afternoon storms build over Rila from mid-June. The Seven Lakes cirque holds snow patches into July.
logistics.bookingWindows: Guesthouses 2-3 weeks; Rila cells 3-4 weeks; the car 4-6 weeks (manual transmission is the default and much cheaper).
logistics.money: Bulgaria has adopted the euro at the fixed rate of 1 EUR = 1.95583 BGN. Mandatory dual EUR/BGN display **ended on 8 August 2026**, so prices are now quoted in euro alone unless a shop chooses to keep the lev figure for reference; the lev itself ceased to be legal tender on 31 January 2026. Cards are widely taken in towns, but cave tickets, village guesthouses and monastery cells are often cash, carry €60, €80 in small notes.
logistics.transportRules: 50 km/h in towns, 90 outside, 140 on motorway. Dipped headlights compulsory year-round, day and night. Alcohol limit 0.5‰. Winter tyres or chains required 15 November-1 March.
logistics.permits: BGTOLL e-vignette on all national roads. Caves are guided-entry only, on fixed departures, with no photography inside some sections; Rila Monastery bans shorts and bare shoulders in the church.

proTips: Do the Devil's Throat on the **first tour of the day**. The hall's acoustics and the waterfall roar are ruined once three groups overlap, and the 301 steps are a bottleneck.
Sleep in Trigrad or Yagodina, not Devin, if you want the caves without the coach window. The villages are half the price of Pamporovo.
Ask your Shiroka Laka host for *"kaba gaida na zhivo"*, live bagpipe. Students and village players do informal evenings; it costs a round of rakia, not a ticket.
Drive the Trigrad gorge before 09:00 or after 17:00. Coach transfers run mid-morning and mid-afternoon, and that is when the single-track reversing happens.
At the Seven Lakes, walk **anti-clockwise to Salzata first**, then descend past Okoto. Everyone else goes the other way and you will meet the crowd head-on rather than travel inside it.
Rila Monastery is a two-hour day trip from Sofia for the coaches. Staying the night costs about the same as a Sofia hotel and buys you dawn in an empty courtyard.
Buy the vignette yourself on bgtoll.bg if you have any doubt. It takes three minutes, costs less than one fine, and the receipt is your evidence.

raw.Driving legs (km + realistic time): Plovdiv→Bachkovo 30 km/40 min (Asenovgrad, road 86); Bachkovo→Devin 105 km/2 h 30 via Krichim and the Vacha reservoir road; Devin→Trigrad 30 km/55 min; Trigrad→Yagodina 35 km/1 h (back to the Teshel junction, then the Buynovo gorge); Yagodina→Shiroka Laka 45 km/1 h 10; Shiroka Laka→Smolyan 25 km/35 min; Smolyan→Momchilovtsi 18 km/30 min; Smolyan→Pamporovo 16 km/25 min over the Prevala saddle; Pamporovo→Batak 120 km/2 h 40 via Devin and Dospat; Batak→Velingrad 35 km/45 min; Velingrad→Rila Monastery 150 km/2 h 45 via Yundola, Razlog, the Predel pass and Kocherinovo; Rila Monastery→Panichishte 70 km/1 h 40; Panichishte→Sofia 80 km/1 h 15.
raw.Passes and hairpins: The **Prevala** saddle between Smolyan and Pamporovo, around 1,600 m, is the loop's high road point and the first to ice. The **Yavorovets** pass carries the Devin-Dospat road over the watershed. The Shiroka Laka-Pamporovo climb stacks roughly twenty-five hairpins in 12 km; the Vacha reservoir road runs 40 km of continuous bends with no straight over 300 m. **Predel** (1,140 m) is the only fast pass on the trip.
raw.Honest width warning: The road into **Trigrad** narrows to effectively single-track between the gorge walls, around 3.5 m at the tightest point, with short unlit rock-cut tunnels, no barrier on the river side and passing places every few hundred metres. Fine in a hatchback at 20 km/h; genuinely unpleasant in a large SUV or campervan, and when a coach comes the other way somebody reverses. The Buynovo gorge road to Yagodina is comparable.
raw.Car rental and vignette: Bulgaria's vignette is fully electronic, bought by number plate through **BGTOLL** (bgtoll.bg, the app, or any petrol-station terminal). No sticker; ANPR cameras enforce it. One-day, weekend, weekly, monthly, quarterly and annual products exist; from **1 August 2026** the car (≤3.5 t) tariff is **one day €5.30, weekend €6.60, week €10.00, month €19.90, quarter €35.90, year €64.50**, a 30% rise on the previous rates, so budget the week's vignette at ten euros rather than the older seven. Rentals normally come vignetted, confirm the plate is registered. Cross-border: most Bulgarian rentals allow Greece and Romania with a Green Card and a fee (€30, €60); **North Macedonia, Serbia and Türkiye are usually excluded or need written authorisation**, with extra insurance bought at the Turkish border.
raw.Fuel: Real gaps up here. Fill in **Devin**, **Smolyan** or **Dospat** and never drop below a quarter tank: no fuel in Trigrad, Yagodina, Shiroka Laka or Momchilovtsi, and Devin-Dospat is 60 km of empty forest road.
raw.Viewpoints: The **Eagle's Eye (Orlovo Oko)** glass platform at about 1,563 m above the Buynovo gorge; the **Snezhanka** TV tower at 1,926 m above Pamporovo; the Rozhen meadows above Momchilovtsi; the Hrelyo's Tower courtyard at Rila; the chairlift top station above the Seven Lakes cirque.
